chart-maker.quickAnswer: Type one label and value per line — like Mon,120 — pick bar, line, or pie, add a title, and the chart renders on a 900 x 600 canvas. Bar height follows the rule height = (value / max) x plotHeight: with values 120, 200, 150, the max is 200, so the bars reach 60, 100, and 75 percent of the plot. Download the PNG for slides and posts.
keyFacts: Three chart types: bar for comparisons, line for trends, pie for shares.
Data entry is plain text: one label,value pair per line, up to 24 points.
Bars and lines scale to the maximum value so the biggest point always fills the plot.
Pie slices are labeled with percentages computed from the total.
Negative values are supported in bar and line charts.
The 900 x 600 PNG is sharp enough for slides, documents, and social posts.
howTo: Pick the chart type: bar, line, or pie.
Type your data as label,value — one pair per line.
Add a chart title and pick the main color.
Check the live preview; fix any red error message about bad lines.
Click Download to save the chart as a PNG image.
chart-maker.formula:
Bar/line scaling: height = (value / maxValue) x plotHeight.
Pie slices: sliceAngle = (value / total) x 360 degrees.
Percent label = value / total x 100.
Example: values 120, 200, 150 -> total 470; pie shares 25.5%, 42.6%, 31.9%.
chart-maker.workedExample:
Data: Mon,120 / Tue,200 / Wed,150. Bar chart, plot height 400 px:
1. maxValue = 200.
2. Mon: 120/200 x 400 = 240 px (60% of plot).
3. Tue: 200/200 x 400 = 400 px (full height).
4. Wed: 150/200 x 400 = 300 px (75% of plot).
5. Pie version: total = 470; Mon = 120/470 = 25.5%, Tue = 42.6%, Wed = 31.9% — slices of 91.9, 153.2, and 114.9 degrees.

faqs.q: How do I enter my data?
faqs.a: One pair per line in the form label,value — for example: Mon,120 on the first line, Tue,200 on the second. Commas separate the label from the number. Decimals like 12.5 work fine.

faqs.q: Which chart type should I use?
faqs.a: Bars compare categories (sales by month). Lines show change over time. Pies show parts of a whole (market share). If your values can be negative, avoid pie — negative slices are meaningless.

faqs.q: Can I compare two data series?
faqs.a: Not in this version — one series per chart. For a comparison, make two charts with the same color and place them side by side in your document or slide.

faqs.q: Why does my pie chart look wrong?
faqs.a: Pie charts need all-positive values that form a meaningful whole. Check for typos like a missing comma (Mon120 is invalid) or negative numbers, and the error message will point at the exact line.

faqs.q: What size is the downloaded image?
faqs.a: 900 x 600 pixels — crisp on screens and fine for printing up to about 7 inches wide. It scales cleanly into PowerPoint, Word, and social posts.
